With the valley isolated by winter blizzards and encroaching dangers, Sten takes it upon himself to outfit green apprentices with sturdy gear before they freeze or wander unprepared into the drifts. Beyond assembling winter outfitting from local wolf hides, Sten serves as an informal postmaster for Coldridge Valley. He handles messages passed through the treacherous Coldridge Pass and distributes official runes, memoranda, and orders to class trainers throughout the basin, ensuring novice warriors, priests, and mages get their instructions despite the hostile trogg presence blocking the tunnels.

npc:tallonkai-swiftroot.text: Tallonkai Swiftroot. Tallonkai Swiftroot is a night elf resident of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Concerned with the emerging corruption tainting the great boughs, he enlists young adventurers to recover enchanted relics and stem the foul forces plaguing the woods. Dwelling in the canopy settlement of Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot keeps a watchful eye over the surrounding woods. Like many night elves living beneath the boughs of the newly grown World Tree, he is alarmed by the unnatural agitation of the wildlife and the unsettling shadows gathering at the edges of their settlements. Tallonkai directs adventurers to confront foul entities disturbing Teldrassil's peace. His concerns include corrupted dream catchers crafted to protect sleeping druids, vicious gnarlpine furbolgs succumbing to a dark malaise, and the corrupted Gnarlpine mystics led by Ferocitas the Dream Eater. To Tallonkai, cleansing these disturbances is crucial to defending the fragile home of the Kaldorei.

npc:verner-osgood.text: Verner Osgood. Verner Osgood is the resident blacksmith of Lakeshire, stationed just outside the town smithy. Balancing local civilian trade with the crushing demands of the Stormwind military, he works tirelessly to keep horses shod and defenders armed amid relentless gnoll raids. Standing by the forge in central Lakeshire, Verner Osgood represents the strained industrial backbone of the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with crafting basic supplies like horseshoes for local mounts, Verner finds his stock constantly co-opted to manufacture weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard. With the kingdom stretching its borders thin and local garrisons lacking supplies, independent smiths like Verner must carry the logistical burden of the realm's defense. Verner's troubles extend far beyond a shortage of iron. The gnolls infesting the Redridge hills routinely ambush livestock, carrying off working horses whenever they stray outside the town perimeter. Driven to exasperation by the destruction of his livelihood, Verner actively recruits traveling adventurers to cull the marauding packs and hunt down their ferocious packleader, Yowler.

npc:viktori-prism-antras.text: Viktori Prism'Antras. Viktori Prism'Antras is an eccentric stargazer residing in a small hillside hut overlooking Darkshire. While the town around him succumbs to dread and looming horrors, Viktori focuses intently on building a telescope to view the heavens clearly. To realize his vision, he relies on adventurous travelers to acquire intricate parts based on gnomish schematics. Perched up the slope just beyond the gryphon roost, Viktori Prism'Antras spends his days peering outward from the gloom of Duskwood. Amid undead incursions, ravenous spiders, and creeping shadows, his obsession lies far beyond the suffocating canopy. He dreams of building a magnificent optical telescope capable of bringing the stars into brilliant focus, offering a quiet escape from the dread that engulfs the hamlet. Constructing such a delicate apparatus is no simple matter in a cursed forest. Viktori works from blueprints provided by his gnomish friend, Cog Glitzspinner. To complete the device, he enlists passersby to track down rare lens-crafting materials and mechanical housings, ranging from finely cut glass to metal lenses scattered across perilous territory.

npc:william-pestle.text: William Pestle. William Pestle is a human alchemist staying inside Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn. Together with his brother Morgan, he helps run the apothecary shop in Stormwind's Trade District. He frequently employs traveling adventurers to gather odd reagents like kobold candles, murloc kelp, and herbal supplies. While his brother Morgan Pestle manages the counter at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District of Stormwind City, William operates out of the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Being stationed in Elwynn Forest allows him to work closely with local gatherers and secure raw materials that city shops constantly require. He maintains regular shipments back to the capital, ensuring Stormwind's citizens have steady access to restorative salves, draughts, and powders. William's craft often demands unusual components that go beyond simple garden herbs. He frequently commissions newcomers to gather wax candles carried by Elwynn's infesting kobolds, as well as crystal kelp taken from the murlocs of Crystal Lake, just east of Goldshire. Although such concoctions seem bizarre to the uninitiated, William insists these strange ingredients possess potent alchemical virtues.

npc:wizbang-cranktoggle.text: Wizbang Cranktoggle. Wizbang Cranktoggle is an eccentric gnome engineer residing on the upper floor of the Auberdine inn. Despite being far from the cog-filled halls of Gnomeregan or Ironforge, he has turned his mechanical ingenuity toward setting up and maintaining automated communication devices known as buzzboxes across the wild coast of Darkshore. While the night elves of Auberdine prefer living in harmony with nature and leaning upon ancient customs, Wizbang Cranktoggle represents the curious, tinkering presence of the Alliance. Perched on the top floor of Auberdine's inn, surrounded by tools and spare components, Wizbang pays little mind to the solemn druidic traditions of Kalimdor, focusing instead on pragmatic mechanical challenges. Wizbang's primary project along Darkshore is deploying and maintaining his peculiar invention: the buzzbox. Designed to establish automated reporting and long-distance communication across the rugged, sprawling coastline, these contraptions often suffer from coastal weathering and the hostility of local wildlife. Wizbang frequently recruits travelers to gather components, salvage tools like gaffer jacks, and recover electropellers to keep his mechanical surveillance functioning.

subzone:alexston-farmstead.text: Alexston Farmstead. The Alexston Farmstead is a derelict farm in Westfall, overgrown and prowled by haywire Harvest Watchers. Once the childhood home of Stormwind's city architect, Baros Alexston, it has fallen into ruin like much of the breadbasket around it. Situated amidst the dry plains of Westfall, the Alexston Farmstead stands as another grim testament to the kingdom's neglect. Like neighboring estates, the farm was abandoned by its caretakers when banditry erupted across the countryside. Today, the fields are overgrown, and the mechanical Harvest Watchers left behind to tend the crops have spun out of control, violently attacking anyone who approaches the barren farmhouse. Despite its bleak state, the farm is tied to one of Stormwind's most prominent citizens. Baros Alexston, the skilled architect who helped design parts of the rebuilt capital, spent his youth toiling on these very fields. He left the farmstead long before the unrest began to pursue his trade in masonry and construction, leaving behind a memento of his early life nestled among the ruins.

subzone:alterac-mountains.text: Alterac Mountains. The Alterac Mountains are a rugged, snow-capped range rising directly above the rolling pastures of Hillsbrad. Once the heart of a proud human kingdom, the slopes now harbor ruined settlements, bandit factions, and dangerous wilderness where travelers rarely walk unguarded. Long before the hills fell into chaos, these highlands formed the sovereign nation of Alterac, one of the seven kingdoms born from ancient Arathor. That legacy shattered during the Second War when King Aiden Perenolde struck a clandestine pact with the Old Horde, allowing orcish forces passage through the peaks in exchange for his kingdom's safety. The Alliance of Lordaeron uncovered the betrayal and deposed Perenolde, leaving the region fractured by martial law and territorial disputes. Following the devastation of the Third War, the mountains collapsed into complete lawlessness. The disinherited nobles of the realm banded together to form the Syndicate, operating out of the ruins of Strahnbrad and plotting to reclaim their lost dominion through sabotage and assassination. Between ruthless Crushridge ogres occupying the shattered capital, marauding gnolls, and the shattered magical ruins around Dalaran, the passes of Alterac remain some of the most perilous pathways in Lordaeron.

subzone:alther-s-mill.text: Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a ruined lumber mill tucked into the rugged hills northeast of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital source of processed timber for local builders, the abandoned grounds have deteriorated into a haven for feral scavengers and prowling predators. For adventurers traveling east toward Stonewatch, the dilapidated structures serve as a grim landmark marking the boundary of safe frontier territory. Before the region fell prey to invading predators and orc raids, Alther's Mill bustled with timber trade that supplied the construction of Lakeshire and surrounding settlements. Its quiet clearing northeast of Lake Everstill provided ready access to mountain timber stands. As turmoil mounted across the kingdom of Stormwind and the Blackrock clan pushed down from the heights of Stonewatch, local millers abandoned the facility, leaving the dry timber buildings and wheel to decay into rot. In the absence of human workers, the mill became infested with monstrous tarantulas, carrion vultures, and opportunistic raiders. Travelers cutting through the path to the eastern passes must skirt its shadowed perimeter carefully. In recent years, shadowy operatives and thieves have also taken advantage of the abandoned compound, using its discarded storage boxes and hidden corners to hone illicit lockpicking crafts and covert trades far from the eyes of the Lakeshire Town Watch.

subzone:anvilmar.text: Anvilmar. Anvilmar is a fortified dwarven outpost nestled in the snowy depths of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. Centered around a massive stone forge, it serves as the primary training grounds and rallying point for young Bronzebeard dwarves and displaced gnomish refugees beginning their adventures. Tucked away in the northern crags of Coldridge Valley, Anvilmar stands as an enduring symbol of dwarven perseverance. Dominated by a roaring central forge, this sturdy masonry complex houses class mentors, supply vendors, and veteran mountain mountaineers who drill recruits before sending them out into the wider kingdom. Though sheltered behind towering drifts, the settlement remains on constant guard against the hostile Frostmane trolls and aggressive wild beasts prowling the frozen valley. The settlement likely takes its proud name from High King Modimus Anvilmar, the ancient sovereign who ruled all dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. However, its history has not been without strife. In bygone days, a towering Frostmane troll managed to breach the perimeter and lay waste to the enclave. Today, the garrison remains vigilant, ensuring the forge fires stay lit and no such disaster ever strikes the starting grounds again.

subzone:astranaar.text: Astranaar. Astranaar is the primary Night Elf settlement in central Ashenvale, built across a serene lake island straddling the ancient forest road. Serving as the beating heart of Alliance operations in the region, it provides vital refuge to travelers facing encroaching threats from hostile furbolgs, satyrs, and the Horde. Situated atop an island in the middle of a forest lake, Astranaar stands as the largest night elven settlement in Ashenvale. Connected to the mainland by wooden footbridges spanning the waters, the town houses sentinels, priests, and artisans who keep vigil over the woodlands. In addition to offering basic comforts such as an inn, traders, and an expert leatherworker, its elevated perches host a flight master providing hippogryph travel to distant outposts across Kalimdor. Despite its tranquil waters and glowing lanterns, Astranaar exists in a state of perpetual readiness. Local leaders like Raene Wolfrunner coordinate patrols and defensive actions against the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs encroaching from the north, fearful they may mount a direct assault on the settlement. The town also bears quiet historical sorrow: across the lake in the cemetery lies the resting place of Valstann Staghelm, who fell a thousand years ago during the War of the Shifting Sands.

subzone:auberdine.text: Auberdine. Auberdine is a coastal night elven port town on the gloomy shores of Darkshore, serving as the Alliance's primary maritime gateway to northern Kalimdor. Sheltered beneath overcast skies and pine-covered bluffs, it connects the island home of Teldrassil to the Eastern Kingdoms while serving as an administrative haven against the encroaching wilderness. Resting along the shores of the Veiled Sea, Auberdine is the only major settlement to successfully endure in modern Darkshore. Unlike the secluded treetop cities of Teldrassil, Auberdine looks outward, serving as the Alliance's busiest port in the north. Regular ships sail between here and Menethil Harbor in the Eastern Kingdoms, while local ferries run to Rut'theran Village at the boughs of the World Tree. Because of its trade role, Auberdine embraces a more cosmopolitan air than traditional elven enclaves; visitors find lamps illuminating stone-laid streets, bilingual signs in Darnassian and Common, and outland merchants including dwarves and gnomes mingling among the low-slung, arched timber houses. Governed by elder Thundris Windweaver and the Auberdine Village Council, the town coordinates the defence of Darkshore alongside the local Sentinels. Despite its role as a vital trade hub, highborn denizens of Darnassus often look askance at Auberdine, viewing its population of traders, fishermen, and outsiders as misfits. The town endures relentless regional perils: aggressive murlocs raid the fishing boats along the strand, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs press from the south, and foul magic seeping down from Felwood agitates the local wildlife.

subzone:azurelode-mine.text: Azurelode Mine. Azurelode Mine is an active Alliance iron mine nestled in the southwestern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills. Guarded by Southshore's militia and worked by human laborers, its steady supply of ore fuels the local human war effort against the Forsaken of Tarren Mill. Situated southwest of the open farmland and just west of Southshore, Azurelode Mine has long tapped into the mineral-rich ridges along the coast. Before the Greymane Wall was sealed, these hills were considered part of Gilnean territory. Today, human miners labor deep underground under the watchful eye of Foreman Bonds, extracting iron to forge arms and armor for the Alliance defenders holding the region against the Undercity. Because Azurelode Mine supplies the bulk of the raw iron needed to maintain Southshore's garrisons and town militia, it sits directly in the crosshairs of the Horde. Tarren Mill has targeted its workforce and guards in an effort to shatter the supply lines that sustain Hillsbrad's human strongholds.

subzone:ban-ethil-barrow-den.text: Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Ban'ethil Barrow Den is a sacred subterranean sanctuary hollowed out within the roots of Teldrassil. Originally created as a resting place for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, the cavern complex has recently fallen into chaos. The corrupted furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe have overrun its chambers, turning a place of peaceful slumber into a perilous den of madness. Barrow dens serve as sacred resting chambers where night elf druids slumber while projecting their spirits into the Emerald Dream. Ban'ethil Barrow Den was dedicated specifically to sheltering the Druids of the Talon as they communed with nature. Divided into upper and lower subterranean chambers, the den once resonated with tranquil reverie and deep meditative magic. However, the affliction sweeping Teldrassil's wildlife did not spare the Gnarlpine furbolgs, who invaded the complex, turning its hollowed halls into a fortified warren. Driven mad by mysterious corruption taking root across the World Tree, the Gnarlpine tribe drove out or endangered the slumbering druids within Ban'ethil. The furbolgs now fiercely guard the winding tunnels, aggressive toward any night elf who approaches. For the defenders of Teldrassil, reclaiming the barrow den is an urgent priority, not merely to drive back the hostile furbolgs, but to protect the vulnerable druids and sacred relics trapped within its lower depths.

subzone:baradin-bay.text: Baradin Bay. Baradin Bay is the expansive body of water lying between the shores of Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. Once vigorously patrolled by the powerful navy of Kul Tiras during the Second War, its waters now conceal treacherous reefs, sunken warships, and hostile aquatic predators. Framed by the coasts of Dun Morogh to the south and Lordaeron to the north, Baradin Bay serves as a vital maritime passage connecting the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. The bay is anchored by busy ports like Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands and Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. However, navigating these waters is perilous: shallow sandbanks, jagged shoals, and dangerous fauna like murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks pose constant threats to sailors and travelers alike. During the Second War, Baradin Bay witnessed heavy naval conflict as the fleets of Kul Tiras clashed with the Horde. Today, grim reminders of those battles litter the coast and the seabed. The shattered hulls of the Kul Tiran Third Fleet—known locally as the Lost Fleet—rest half-submerged along the Wetlands coast, while other vessels have plummeted down to Drowned Reef. Hostile spirits, opportunistic salvagers, and ravenous sea beasts now haunt the waters surrounding these decaying timber ruins.

subzone:bathran-s-haunt.text: Bathran's Haunt. Bathran's Haunt is an ancient kaldorei ruin nestled in northwestern Ashenvale, east of the Zoram Strand. Recently, Forsaken herbalists and their guardians have overtaken the site to harvest local flora for their alchemical research, steadily withering the surrounding woodland. North of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, crumbling night elf pillars stand swallowed by thick Ashenvale foliage. What was once a tranquil kaldorei relic has fallen under the shadow of the Forsaken. Skulking among the broken marble, undead herbalists and their enforcers have set up a crude open-air laboratory. Their presence alone blights the ancient soil: grass rots into a sickly brown, vibrant blossoms wilt, and an unnatural decay creeps through the grove as they methodically harvest rare woodland reagents for their experiments. The primary draw of these ruins is Bathran's Hair, a unique remedial herb found taking root only among these particular stones. While night elf and Alliance scouts view the Forsaken presence as a vile desecration of sacred elven soil, the undead work diligently to extract the plant's potent properties. The Horde maintains a vested interest in the compound's botanical yield, though the Forsaken's secretive methods and the resulting corruption of the earth draw suspicion from outsiders and allies alike.

subzone:beggar-s-haunt.text: Beggar's Haunt. Beggar's Haunt is an abandoned Stormwind scout tower perched on a hillside in northeastern Duskwood, near the mountain road to Deadwind Pass. While originally built to keep watch over the kingdom's eastern borders, it has become an outpost for Forsaken infiltrators deep within Alliance territory. Perched above the foggy hills east of Manor Mistmantle, Beggar's Haunt was once an active observation post manned by the Stormwind Guard to secure the eastern approaches to the realm. As Grand Hamlet collapsed into the gloom of modern Duskwood and kingdom patrols withdrew to Darkshire, the stone tower was abandoned to the elements. Today, its commanding vantage point serves a far more sinister purpose: agents of the Forsaken, including members of the Royal Apothecary Society and Deathstalkers, use the ruined stronghold to conduct research and monitor the region under the Alliance's nose. Behind the tower, a steep, twisting path descends to a secluded pool and waterfall known as Knight's Hollow. Here lies an unmarked grave flanked by two ominous hooded stone statues resembling the guardians flanking the Dark Portal. Nearby resting plots, including the burial site of an Unknown Soldier, speak to forgotten clashes fought along this frontier long before the Forsaken moved into the watchtower.

subzone:boulderslide-ravine.text: Boulderslide Ravine. Boulderslide Ravine is a rugged, secluded canyon tucked away in the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via Webwinder Path. Largely spared from the direct clashes between the Horde and Alliance, it serves as the rocky approach to Boulderslide Cavern and remains home to wild mountain beasts. Tucked away off Webwinder Path, Boulderslide Ravine is a narrow cut of rock in the Stonetalon heights. While loggers, night elves, and the Horde battle over timber and sacred glades throughout the region, this craggy pass remains relatively undisturbed by military forces. Wild mountain rams and roaming crag beasts like Cliff Stormers make up the local fauna, navigating the treacherous ledges and sheer stone walls. Prospectors also keep an eye on the ravine, as rich mineral veins frequently crop up along the rocky slopes leading deeper toward the cavern network. Opposite the entrance to Boulderslide Cavern lies a small, quiet cave overlooking the ravine. Lit by rough torches and stacked with weathered supply barrels, the shelter contains primitive tribal paintings across its interior walls. The crude artwork bears a striking resemblance to ancient tauren designs, suggesting that native tribes traveled or sought temporary shelter in these crags long before modern conflict swept into the mountains.

subzone:camp-aparaje.text: Camp Aparaje. Camp Aparaje was once a peaceful tauren village nestled in the eastern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Today, it lies overrun and occupied by the hostile Grimtotem tribe, who slaughtered the original settlers and took the outpost for themselves. Perched along the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, Camp Aparaje was established by peaceful tauren looking to live quietly in the highlands. That tranquility was shattered when raiders from the nearby Grimtotem Post, led by Grundig Darkcloud, launched a brutal and unprovoked assault. The villagers were butchered or driven away, and survivors such as Makaba Flathoof were left mourning the destruction of their home while dreading the fate of captive kin. Now completely occupied by Grimtotem warriors, Camp Aparaje serves as a forward base of operations for the aggressive tribe in the region. Unlike typical Grimtotem settlements that fly blue markings, the great totem standing in Aparaje is carved with deep crimson paint.

subzone:canals-stormwind-city.text: Canals (Stormwind City). The Canals are a network of stone-lined waterways weaving through Stormwind City, separating its distinct districts. They serve as quiet thoroughfares for pedestrians and anglers, while quietly harboring hidden hazards and the entrance to the city's prison. The Canals link and define the districts of Stormwind, dividing the bustling markets of the Trade District from the aged alleys of Old Town, the cathedral gardens, and the Dwarven District. Stone bridges, archways, and waterside walkways frame quiet establishments like the Gallina Winery, tailor shops, and quiet residential homes. In addition to serving local merchants and recreational fishermen, the waterways conceal the fortified entrance to the Stockade, where Stormwind's most dangerous criminals and rebels are held beneath street level. The placid surface of the waterways belies a violent past. Following the sack of Stormwind during the First War, the canals were discovered choked with rubble, timber, and the corpses of slaughtered defenders. When the Alliance of Lordaeron liberated the ruins, soldiers undertook the grim labor of clearing the waterways and burying the dead before rebuilding began. Today, while cleaned and restored, the depths retain an air of mystery, fueled by city rumors of a massive albino crocolisk prowling beneath the docks.

subzone:cathedral-of-light.text: Cathedral of Light. The Cathedral of Light is the spiritual heart of Stormwind City and the primary sanctuary of the Church of the Holy Light. Standing tall over Cathedral Square, it serves as the central bastion for human priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Rebuilt after its devastation during the First War under the guidance of Archbishop Alonsus Faol and then-Bishop Benedictus, the Cathedral of Light stands as a towering beacon of resilience. Its vast halls and subterranean catacombs sheltered desperate refugees during the darkest hours of Stormwind's reconstruction. With the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge during the Third War, the seat of the Church shifted south to Stormwind. Today, Archbishop Benedictus shepherds the faithful from this grand hall, providing spiritual guidance to the entire Alliance. Beyond serving as a house of prayer and healing, the cathedral acts as the primary headquarters for the remaining Knights of the Silver Hand in the southern kingdoms. High-ranking figures such as Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker and Duthorian Rall train promising squires through the sacred trials of the Tome of Valor and the Tome of Divinity. Alongside them, High Priestess Laurena guides devout acolytes in the deepest tenets of the Light, preparing holy champions to defend the realm against the rising threat of the Defias Brotherhood and the Scourge.

subzone:cathedral-square.text: Cathedral Square. Cathedral Square is the spiritual and civic heart of Stormwind City, dominated by the majestic Cathedral of Light. Beyond serving as a place of worship and devotion, the bustling plaza houses municipal institutions like City Hall, the city orphanage, and the regional headquarters of the Argent Dawn. Situated northwest of the Trade District and southeast of the Dwarven District, Cathedral Square serves as the epicenter of faith in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Dominating the skyline is the Cathedral of Light, the preeminent sanctuary for followers of the Holy Light across Azeroth. Priests, paladins, and healers gather here to study, pray, and train. Citizens, pilgrims, and local schoolchildren led by School Mistress Danna regularly mingle in the square for conversation and contemplation. The district is not merely reserved for prayer; it is one of the capital's busiest civic centers. The square houses the Stormwind Orphanage as well as City Hall, anchoring the administrative life of the kingdom. Specialized armorers and weaponsmiths catering to holy crusaders, such as Righteous Plates and Just Maces, line the avenues. It also serves as the base of operations for the Argent Dawn within Stormwind, where recruiters and representatives coordinate relief efforts and rally champions against the encroaching threats of the Scourge in the northern kingdoms.

subzone:cenarion-enclave.text: Cenarion Enclave. The Cenarion Enclave is the verdant northwestern district of Darnassus, serving as the central gathering place and seat of power for the Cenarion Circle in the capital. While Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage lies slumbering within the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the night elven druids from the great hollows and living boughs of this grove. Occupying a high terrace above the Temple Gardens, the Cenarion Enclave is shaped from ancient oaks and ashes marked with runic bark. Convocations of the Cenarion Circle gather within structures molded directly from living wood and stone. With Malfurion Stormrage absent in the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm oversees affairs here, pushing his ambitious vision for Teldrassil despite lingering political friction with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Beyond the druids who meditate among its streams, the enclave also hosts the capital's elven hunters and the stables where skilled riders learn to tame Darnassian nightsabers. Though renowned as a tranquil sanctuary of nature, the enclave harbors more covert activities. Beneath the hollowed roots of the westernmost bough lies a subterranean refuge used by Darnassus's clandestine rogues, who conduct their quiet business shielded by the rustling canopy above.

subzone:charred-vale.text: Charred Vale. The Charred Vale is a smoldering valley in southwestern Stonetalon Mountains, devastated by the reckless deforestation and machinery of the Venture Company. Once a thriving haven for treants and chimaeras, it is now engulfed in flames, roving elementals, and hostile harpies. Not long ago, this southwest basin was a flourishing alpine wood guarded by majestic treants and inhabited by native chimaeras and harpies. Its ruin began with the arrival of the Venture Company. The greedy goblin outfit clear-cut the forest with explosive machinery, corrupting the guardians and awakening chaotic fire elementals. Though the treants eventually forced the goblins back, the land was left broken, scarred by fire, and tainted by whatever foul devices the retreating loggers deployed. Today, blackened ancients wander blindly through smoke and ash alongside enraged elementals. Bloodfury harpies roost in the skeletal snags, defending what remains of their territory. Despite the hostility of the valley, druids from Sun Rock Retreat refuse to abandon the region, dispatching travelers to sow enchanted seeds and tend the corrupted ancients in a persistent campaign to reclaim the scorched earth.

subzone:clean-zone.text: Clean Zone. The Clean Zone is a fortified, decontamination enclave nestled inside the ruined city of Gnomeregan just past the upper Hall of Gears. It serves as the sole safe haven within the irradiated facility where uncorrupted gnomish forces hold ground against surrounding troggs and leper gnomes. Here, field medics, technicians, and specialized Sparklematic machines offer respite and salvage operations amid the radioactive ruins. While most of Gnomeregan succumbed to Mekkatorque's disastrous venting of radioactive waste, the Clean Zone remains untainted. Positioned strategically between the trogg-infested Dormitory below and the contested corridors of the Hall of Gears above, it acts as a fortified forward base. Resolute gnome defenders, technicians, and field medics hold the barricades day and night, ensuring Alliance expeditions have a stable staging ground to regroup, mend wounds, and maintain machinery. Beyond serving as a military redoubt, the Clean Zone is a hub for salvaging the lost capital. Gnomish engineers installed Sparklematic 5200 units to chemically scrub and wash grime-encrusted relics hauled out of the city's radioactive underbelly. Technicians and merchants like Tink Sprocketwhistle process these reclaimed gears and baubles, outfitting adventurers while studying the lingering toxic fallout that plagues the deep tunnels.

subzone:cleft.text: Cleft. The Cleft is a darkened hollow located northwest of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a tranquil corner of the boughs, it has been claimed by the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs, who use it as a stronghold to ambush travelers moving along the main highway toward Darnassus. Situated off the highway between Dolanaar and Darnassus, the Cleft has turned into one of the most perilous dens on the world tree. Driven mad by the foul taint spreading through Teldrassil, the resident Gnarlpine furbolgs have fortified this hollow. From this redoubt, the maddened beasts terrorize the local roads, threatening to cut Dolanaar off from the capital.

subzone:command-center.text: Command Center. The Command Center, often referred to as the Stormwind Barracks, stands in the heart of Old Town as the operational headquarters for the city's military officers. In peacetime, it houses the standing army, but with Stormwind's forces dispatched to distant frontiers, it currently operates with a seasoned skeleton crew focused on drilling recruits and local militia. Situated within the weathered streets of Old Town, the Command Center serves as the primary garrison and martial training ground for the kingdom of Stormwind. Normally packed with regular infantry and ranking officers, the facility is uncharacteristically sparse. With much of the royal army committed to campaigns abroad, the barracks relies on a veteran cadre of instructors—including Ander Germaine and martial artist Wu Shen—to train fresh warriors to bolster the city's defenses. Guards throughout Stormwind often direct newcomers to the 'Barracks' when seeking instruction in heavy arms and tactical combat. The building's proximity to both the Pig and Whistle Tavern and the shadowy operations elsewhere in Old Town makes it an essential anchor of order in a district known for tavern brawls and roguish activity.

subzone:commons.text: Commons. The Commons serves as the vibrant commercial heart of Ironforge, connecting the city entrance directly to its vast caverns. Teeming with merchants, travelers, and bankers, it is the busiest thoroughfare in the dwarven capital and the central marketplace for the entire Alliance. Located just northeast of the Gates of Ironforge, the Commons is the first district that greets travelers entering the mountain kingdom. Carved directly out of the stone, this bustling market street houses the primary Alliance Auction House, the Stonefire Tavern, and the city's central bank within the Vault of Ironforge. Broad avenues connect it seamlessly to the Great Forge, the Mystic Ward, and the Military Ward, ensuring that nearly all foot traffic in the mountain passes through its bustling storefronts. Due to Ironforge's central location on the Eastern Kingdoms continent and its direct underground Deeprun Tram link to Stormwind, the Commons functions as the Alliance's primary trade nexus. Adventurers converge here to trade goods brought from every corner of Azeroth, purchase armaments from merchants like Steelfury and Barim, or meet under the warm lantern light of the local inn before heading out into the Khaz Modan snows.

subzone:craftsmen-s-terrace.text: Craftsmen's Terrace. The Craftsmen's Terrace is the bustling artisan district situated in the northern reaches of Darnassus. It serves as the primary trade and manufacturing hub for the night elf capital, housing workshops, profession trainers, and a lively inn. The district also hosts external representatives, including an embassy for the neutral Argent Dawn. Spanning the northern edge of the canopy city, the Craftsmen's Terrace gathers the diverse trades that keep Darnassus running. Woodworkers, leathercrafters, alchemists, and other artisans operate their shops here, integrating classic night elven methods with practical craft. The district also provides essential community amenities, including an inn, a guild master, and guild petition vendors. Bridges connect the terrace directly to the Cenarion Enclave to the west and the Warrior's Terrace to the south. Despite the kaldorei's historic isolation, the Craftsmen's Terrace is home to foreign connections, most notably an embassy established by the Argent Dawn to coordinate with northern allies against the Scourge. Visitors browsing the district's various workshops might also stumble across scattered scholarly volumes, ranging from historical accounts of the War of the Ancients to chronicles detailing the Second War and esoteric treatises on the Old Gods.

subzone:cragpool-lake.text: Cragpool Lake. Cragpool Lake is a body of water tucked inside Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looming above its dark waters sits a massive timber structure erected by the Venture Company. Nestled within Windshear Crag, Cragpool Lake lies directly beneath the towering logging apparatus built by the Venture Company. An enormous wooden structure spans above the water, serving as the vantage point from which Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle oversees operations across the mountain valley. Venture Company workers occupy the platforms overhead.

subzone:dagger-hills.text: Dagger Hills. The Dagger Hills form a rugged ridge rising across southern Westfall, directly behind the blighted town of Moonbrook. Long neglected by the crown, this rocky highland serves as a hostile hideout for cutthroats, bandits, and creeping terrors that threaten the surrounding plains. Rising high above the dilapidated settlement of Moonbrook, the Dagger Hills mark the jagged southern reaches of Westfall. Stripped of official royal patrols from Stormwind, this arid highland has become a natural fortification for the Defias Brotherhood. Knuckledusters, pathstalkers, and highwaymen lurk among the rocky crests and scrub, ambushing unwary travelers and keeping watch over the approaches to their strongholds below. Beyond mortal outlaws, the Dagger Hills carry an eerie reputation under cover of darkness. The unsettling specter Leprithus, a wandering ghoul, has been sighted stalking the desolate heights when the sun dips. Aside from wandering outlaws and lingering undead, the only resident willing to brave the ridge is Grimbooze Thunderbrew, a dwarven brewer who sets up his distilling equipment in the rugged wilderness regardless of the nearby dangers.

subzone:darkshire.text: Darkshire. Darkshire, formerly known as Grand Hamlet, is a battered settlement in eastern Duskwood. Cloaked in an enduring, unnatural gloom and neglected by Stormwind, the town survives only through the vigilance of the Night Watch and the stubborn endurance of its people. Once a peaceful woodland settlement called Grand Hamlet, the village was razed by the Old Horde during the First War and later rebuilt. Its fortune turned truly bitter following the fall of Medivh at Karazhan, whose lingering death throes cursed Brightwood into the shadowy wilderness now called Duskwood. Despite being a nominal holding of the Kingdom of Stormwind, the town hall receives virtually no aid from the crown. Political paralysis in Stormwind City has left the garrison unstaffed and the borders unpatrolled, forcing Mayor Ello Ebonlocke and the local council to administer their own harsh, insular justice in the shadows. Surrounded by walking dead from the western graveyards and feral worgen hunting through the woods, Darkshire clings to life along its palisades. The town's primary shield is the Night Watch, a voluntary civilian militia commanded by Althea Ebonlocke. Operating out of the town square and patrolling the pitch-black thoroughfares, these weary sentries keep the town's roads open and turn back the terrors prowling the tree line. Travelers arriving at the Scarlet Raven Tavern find the locals suspicious, frightened, and desperate for any mercenary capable of holding a blade.

subzone:demon-fall-canyon.text: Demon Fall Canyon. Demon Fall Canyon is a scarred, fel-corrupted gorge situated in southern Ashenvale. It marks the legendary battleground where Grommash Hellscream and Thrall confronted the pit lord Mannoroth, ending the demonic blood curse that had enslaved the orcish race for a generation. Carved into the rugged southern borders of Ashenvale near Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Ridge, this canyon bears the heavy scars of the Third War. It was here that Warchief Thrall and chieftain Grommash Hellscream tracked down the pit lord Mannoroth to break his hold over the Horde. During the fierce duel, Mannoroth incapacitated Thrall, but Grom seized the opening to drive his axe, Gorehowl, straight into the demon's chest. The resulting infernal explosion shattered the pit lord and slew Grom as well, permanently liberating the orcs from their lingering demonic servitude. Following Mannoroth's demise, the Horde dubbed the canyon to commemorate Grom's final stand, erecting a monument nearby to honor his redemption. Despite the pit lord's destruction, his violent death unleashed raw demonic power that thoroughly tainted the surrounding land. Today, the canyon remains saturated in fel magic and crawls with hostile lingering lesser demons, making any pilgrimage to this hallowed ground a perilous venture.

subzone:demon-fall-ridge.text: Demon Fall Ridge. Demon Fall Ridge is a blighted highland in south-eastern Ashenvale, overlooking the canyon where Mannoroth fell. Swarming with lesser demons and corrupting magic, the ridge centers around a desecrated night elf barrow den claimed by the Burning Legion. Rising directly west and above Demon Fall Canyon, Demon Fall Ridge is stained with lingering fel residue from the Third War. While the canyon below marks the site of the catastrophic clash between Grommash Hellscream and the pit lord Mannoroth, this high ground serves as a staging area for surviving demonic invaders. Lesser demons patrol the rocky cliffs, defiling the ancient woodland and threatening any travelers traversing the southern border of Ashenvale. Carved into the side of the ridge rests an abandoned night elf barrow den, hollowed out and converted into a stronghold of dark sorcery. Rather than slumbering druids, the subterranean passages teem with fel fiends. Deep in the subterranean depths lurks Diathorus the Seeker, a cunning dreadlord who rules over this conclave, directing the remaining demonic remnants throughout the forest.

subzone:demont-s-place.text: Demont's Place. Demont's Place is a ruined homestead nestled in southwestern Westfall, just west of the forsaken town of Moonbrook. Once a working agricultural plot, the farm was driven to ruin alongside the rest of the region and claimed by the rogue agents of the Defias Brotherhood. Today, its weathered fences and empty fields stand as another casualty of the realm's fading prosperity. Situated within sight of Moonbrook and the rotting expanse of the Dead Acre, Demont's Place was once among the private family holdings feeding the Kingdom of Stormwind. Economic collapse and the sudden rise of outlaw brigands stripped the farm of its livelihood, forcing out its original caretakers. Much like its neighboring fields, the plot has degenerated into a rough hideout, overrun by outlaws using its weathered grounds as an extension of the Defias stronghold in Moonbrook. Because of its close proximity to Moonbrook, Demont's Place serves the Defias Brotherhood as an operational outpost on the outskirts of their regional center. Thugs, cutpurses, and displaced laborers linger among the fences and shattered structures, ambushing travelers who wander off the southern roads. Until Moonbrook is reclaimed and the outlaws broken, the ground remains far too dangerous for peaceful farming to ever return.

subzone:dormitory.text: Dormitory. The Dormitory is a residential sector within the fallen technological capital of Gnomeregan. Once providing living quarters for countless gnome citizens, it now lies choked with radioactive fallout and crawls with savage, irradiated troggs. Situated just past the decontamination chambers of the Clean Zone, the Dormitory formerly housed the inventors, laborers, and families of Gnomeregan. When High Tinker Mekkatorque initiated the emergency radiation venting to combat the invading trogg horde, this densely populated sector became a trap. Today, its communal halls and living units are completely abandoned by gnomish life, occupied instead by mutated troggs that thrive in the radioactive miasma. Travelers descending toward the lower levels of the city must fight through this tragic reminder of the catastrophe to reach the lower Hall of Gears. Amid the abandoned living quarters, remnants of the city's administrative apparatus still function. The Matrix Punchograph 3005-B machines process security punch cards. These terminals provide clearance for higher-security data terminals deeper within Gnomeregan, helping recover important records left behind when the gnomes fled.

subzone:dun-algaz.text: Dun Algaz. Dun Algaz is the fortified mountain pass and network of tunnels connecting Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Historically contested during the Second War, this vital trade artery has recently fallen under siege by Dragonmaw orcs, cutting off easy transit between Ironforge's territories and Menethil Harbor. Dun Algaz predates the War of the Three Hammers, originally serving as the passage the Wildhammer clan used to migrate north after being driven out of Ironforge. Carved deep into the jagged peaks separating Loch Modan and the Wetlands, the pass consists of sweeping stone tunnels, bastions, and watchposts. Its strategic value cannot be overstated: whoever holds Dun Algaz commands the only overland highway linking the dwarven heartlands to the western sea at Menethil Harbor. During the Second War, the Old Horde retreated to Dun Algaz after their defeat at Dun Modr, turning it into their final southern bulwark against Sir Anduin Lothar's forces. Years later, Nekros Skullcrusher sheltered the Dragonmaw clan in the surrounding caves. Though the Alliance reclaimed the pass for a time, Dragonmaw orcs have once again overrun the stronghold, forcing the dwarven Mountaineers to retreat to the upper tunnels and turning the mountain corridor into a deadly gauntlet for travelers.

subzone:dun-garok.text: Dun Garok. Dun Garok is a fortified dwarven mountain bastion situated in the southeastern heights of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the outpost's stalwart garrison defends regional Alliance interests and nearby operations like the Azurelode Mine against hostile encroachment. To the Forsaken of Tarren Mill, this entrenched dwarven stronghold stands as a constant military threat bordering their domain. Carved into the craggy southeastern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills, Dun Garok stands as a heavily defended redoubt of Ironforge mountaineers and riflemen. Commanded by Captain Ironhill, the dwarves here maintain a critical defensive perimeter, shielding human settlements in Hillsbrad and securing vital operations at the Azurelode Mine. Their sturdy stone architecture and deep entrenchments provide the Alliance with an anchor against nearby threats. Because of its close proximity to Tarren Mill, Dun Garok is viewed by the Forsaken as an intolerable intrusion on their southern border. Sylvanas Windrunner's forces loathe the presence of heavily armed dwarven troops so close to their stronghold, routinely plotting to infiltrate the fortress, break its defenses, and eliminate Captain Ironhill's garrison to secure Forsaken dominion over Hillsbrad.

subzone:dun-modr.text: Dun Modr. Dun Modr is an ancient fortified dwarven town in northern Wetlands, guarding the southern approach to the Thandol Span. Once a critical fortress held and contested across multiple wars, it has recently fallen to a hostile force of Dark Iron dwarves. Situated at the northern edge of the Wetlands, Dun Modr commands the primary overland highway linking Khaz Modan with the northern human kingdoms. Because of this vital location, the stronghold has seen heavy bloodshed over the decades. During the Second War, the Orcish Horde captured and entrenched themselves within the dwarven fortress, using it as a forward staging ground to launch raids and repel Alliance armies. Stromgarde warriors launched a brutal amphibious assault from Tol Barad to reclaim it, only for the Orcs to strike back in a bloody tug-of-war. Alliance forces led by Lord Anduin Lothar ultimately drove the invaders south across the Thandol Span, restoring dwarven custody over the bastion. With Ironforge's attention divided and many of its finest mountaineers committed to Alliance duties abroad, Dun Modr was left vulnerable. Seizing the opportunity, Dark Iron invaders pushed north and sabotaged the Thandol Span with explosives before swarming the fortress. Under the command of the Dark Iron warlock Balgaras the Foul, these infiltrators overran the town's defenders, driving out the Bronzebeard garrison and transforming the strategic outpost into a hostile den. Surrounding Mountaineers now maintain a grim perimeter just down the road, desperately seeking aid to dislodge the occupiers.

subzone:durnholde-keep.text: Durnholde Keep. Durnholde Keep is a shattered fortress situated east of Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Once the nerve center of the Alliance's orc internment camps and the place where Warchief Thrall was raised as a captive gladiator, it now lies in ruin, occupied by outlaws of the Syndicate. Built by the Alliance, Durnholde served as the headquarters overseeing the southern internment camps following the Second War. Commanded by the ambitious and corrupt Lieutenant General Aedelas Blackmoore, it functioned as both an administrative fortress and a gladiatorial arena. It was here that Blackmoore raised the orphaned infant Go'el, naming him Thrall and training him to fight for sport and profit. Aided by Taretha Foxton, Thrall escaped captivity and later united the dispersed orc clans under the banner of the new Horde. Returning to Durnholde, Thrall laid siege to the fortress, slew Blackmoore, and called upon the earth spirits to shatter its walls. Since its collapse prior to the Third War, Durnholde Keep has remained a scarred heap of masonry. In the vacuum left by Lordaeron's fall, the aristocratic bandits of the Syndicate took refuge among the ramparts. Operating out of the broken bailey and towers, these dispossessed Alterac nobles and cutthroats prey upon travelers across the Hillsbrad Foothills, turning a former instrument of martial law into a heavily fortified rogue outpost.

subzone:dwarven-district.text: Dwarven District. Tucked into the northern corner of Stormwind City, the Dwarven District is a bustling industrial enclave filled with roaring furnaces, ringing anvils, and thick smog. Established by Ironforge craftsmen who arrived to help rebuild the capital after the Second War, it serves as the beating mechanical heart of the city. After the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard sent hundreds of dwarven artisans, stonemasons, and engineers south to assist their human allies in rebuilding Stormwind. Rather than dispersing throughout the capital, they established their own enclave in the northern quarter. Today, the district retains the unmistakable character of Ironforge, dominated by heavy stone masonry, sprawling smelting operations, and bustling craft shops. Shops such as Potts' Plates provide a familiar haven for craftspeople from Khaz Modan. It also houses the Stormwind portal to the Deeprun Tram, tethering the human capital directly to Ironforge.

subzone:eastvale-logging-camp.text: Eastvale Logging Camp. Eastvale Logging Camp is a vital lumber settlement tucked into the eastern woodlands of Elwynn Forest, near the border with the Redridge Mountains. The camp supplies vital timber to Stormwind and surrounding settlements, but its operations are constantly hampered by hungry predators prowling the surrounding forests. Orders for timber constantly stream into Eastvale Logging Camp from buyers across the Kingdom of Stormwind, but meeting these strict deadlines is a harrowing task. The dense wilderness surrounding the camp swarms with vicious wolves and prowling bears that routinely chase lumberjacks away from their worksites, leaving valuable cut timber abandoned in the woods. Under the direction of Supervisor Raelen, the camp frequently relies on wandering adventurers to cull the encroaching beasts and retrieve fallen wood before deliveries fall fatally behind schedule. Despite its remote location, Eastvale is more than just a logging outpost. It features several residential dwellings and bustling horse stables where travelers can purchase fine mounts. The lumber trade here is closely tied to Stormwind nobility, including Lord Joran Tremaind, whose family maintains significant business interests in the camp's timber harvest. On a nearby hill overlooking the worksite sits the quiet manor of retired Marshal Haggard, the former leader of the Stormwind Guard, who withdrew to this rustic outpost to live out his retirement away from capital politics.

subzone:echo-ridge-mine.text: Echo Ridge Mine. Echo Ridge Mine is a small excavation carved into the northwestern cliffs of Northshire Valley. Rich in stone and ore, it has recently fallen into the clutches of a destructive kobold infestation, halting Northshire's local operations. Tucked away in the hills above Northshire Abbey, Echo Ridge Mine was meant to supply the valley with useful stone and metal. Instead, opportunistic kobolds swarmed through the tunnels, driving out the local workers. Marshal McBride views the infestation as an unacceptable security risk to Northshire's safety and recruitment efforts, directing new recruits straight into the tunnels to cull their numbers and reclaim the site. The occupation of Echo Ridge is part of a broader pattern of kobold encroachment spreading across Elwynn Forest. If left unchecked in the northwestern ridge, these subterranean pests threaten to disrupt Northshire's peaceful training grounds and choke off crucial resources from reaching the abbey.

subzone:engineering-labs.text: Engineering Labs. The Engineering Labs are a multi-tiered research and manufacturing facility deep within Gnomeregan. Connected to the Workshop Entrance and Launch Bay, this bustling center of gnome innovation was overrun during the city's radioactive cataclysm and is now swarming with crazed leper gnomes and rogue mechanical contraptions. Built around a central mechanical structure, the Engineering Labs span two primary tiers connected by a central cargo lift. In Gnomeregan's prime, tinkerers here developed schematics and fine-tuned clockwork inventions. Today, radiation leaks have driven the remaining researchers mad, transforming them into deranged leper gnomes who mindlessly guard malfunctioning machinery alongside rogue constructs. Beyond its historical role as a laboratory, the chamber serves as a vital transit hub through the lower reaches of the ruined city. Passages wind toward the Launch Bay, Tinkers' Court, and the Workshop Entrance back door. The lower floor also houses the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D terminals, critical processing units required to decipher the coded punch cards carried by gnome engineers.

subzone:falfarren-river.text: Falfarren River. The Falfarren River flows northeast to southwest through the heart of Ashenvale, originating on the slopes of Mount Hyjal before slipping underground beneath the Barrens' northern mountains. It forms a natural boundary between night elven domains around Astranaar to the west and the encroaching Horde outposts to the east. Travelers must tread carefully, as its shaded banks and shallows harbor hostile wildlife and mark the edge of open conflict. Feeding down from Mount Hyjal, the waters of the Falfarren cascade across waterfalls into Xavian before winding between Splintertree Post and Night Run. While it is neither exceptionally deep nor impassable under ordinary weather, it serves as the rough geopolitical dividing line in central Ashenvale. To the west lie Astranaar and the core holdings of the Kaldorei; to the east sit the camps and lumber operations of the Horde. Crossing the main road's wooden bridges brings travelers into the contested heart of the forest, where patrols clash along the banks. Beyond the tensions of warring sentinels and grunts, the river conceals natural and unnatural dangers beneath its surface. Downstream near Felfire Hill, corrupted bog beasts and aggressive water creatures prowl the muddy shallows. Rainfall can swell the currents, yet the true peril lies in the dense canopies flanking either shore, where ambushes and skirmishes routinely spill into the stream.

subzone:fargodeep-mine.text: Fargodeep Mine. Fargodeep Mine is an abandoned gold mine nestled in central Elwynn Forest, south of Goldshire. Once a productive source of wealth for the Kingdom of Stormwind, it has recently been overrun by a belligerent clan of kobolds. Fargodeep Mine once provided steady gold to Stormwind's treasury, but the Kingdom's dwindling military presence in Elwynn has left outlying resources vulnerable. Kobolds quickly swarmed into the dark tunnels, establishing a bustling warren beneath the hills. Marshal Dughan and the local authorities in Goldshire view the infestation with deep concern, not only because of lost ore, but because the emboldened creatures now threaten nearby farmsteads like the Stonefield and Maclure holdings. The mine spans multiple levels, with the lower shafts winding deep beneath the forest floor. Kobold laborers and vermin scurry along the wooden scaffolds, fiercely guarding their scavenged wax and gold dust. Deeper within lurks Goldtooth, a particularly cunning kobold leader known for hoarding trinkets pilfered from unwary travelers and surrounding residents.

subzone:farstrider-lodge.text: Farstrider Lodge. Farstrider Lodge is a hunting outpost in southeastern Loch Modan. Its architecture appears to be high elven, while its residents include the high elf Vyrin Swiftwind, dwarves, and humans. Hunters and travelers come here for training, supplies, and work in the surrounding wilds. Farstrider Lodge stands apart from the sturdy stone buildings typical of Khaz Modan. Its architecture suggests high elven craftsmanship. Vyrin Swiftwind is the only known high elf still residing here, alongside dwarves and humans. The lodge's founder and date of construction are not established. Situated in the southeastern hills of Loch Modan, the lodge serves hunters and travelers exploring the surrounding wilderness. Hunter and pet trainers work here alongside merchants and people seeking help with local wildlife.

subzone:fel-rock.text: Fel Rock. Fel Rock is a blighted cavern hidden within the woods just north of Dolanaar on the boughs of Teldrassil. Once a tranquil hollow, it has fallen into corruption under the influence of the satyr Lord Melenas and his horde of vicious grells. Tucked away in the forested hills north of Dolanaar, Fel Rock was once an ordinary, peaceful cavern carved into the wood and stone of Teldrassil. Today, it stands as an unsettling reminder of the creeping taint encroaching on the world tree. Twisted roots and unnatural shadows dominate the cavern interior, overrun by swarms of wild grells and grellkin. The corruption within Fel Rock stems from the presence of Lord Melenas, a wicked satyr who has claimed the hollow as a stronghold. From deep within the cave, he orchestrates the spread of malevolent corruption right under the watchful gaze of the night elf sentinels. Druids from Dolanaar, particularly Tallonkai Swiftroot, actively enlist capable defenders to cleanse the cave and slay Melenas before his foul blight can spread further into the surrounding woodlands.

subzone:felfire-hill.text: Felfire Hill. Felfire Hill is a blighted, demon-infested rise nestled in eastern Ashenvale. Struck by falling infernals during the Third War, its corrupted soil still burns with demonic power. The Horde maintains fortified guard posts on the bridges leading into the hill to safeguard their nearby settlements. During the cataclysmic invasion of the Third War, flaming meteors fell across Kalimdor as the Burning Legion unleashed its dread infernals. Several of those fiery behemoths struck this ridge in Ashenvale, scouring away the ancient woodlands and corrupting the earth itself. Today, the scorched landscape remains saturated with fel energy and prowled by lingering demons who survived the Legion's defeat at Mount Hyjal. Situated southeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of the Warsong Lumber Camp, Felfire Hill sits uncomfortably close to vital Horde operations. Because the demonic remnants threaten to spill out into the surrounding forest, Horde forces have erected fortified barricades and guard towers at both bridges approaching the hill, containing the foul creatures within their blighted haven.

subzone:fire-scar-shrine.text: Fire Scar Shrine. Fire Scar Shrine is a despoiled night elf shrine nestled in the southwestern forests of Ashenvale. Once a serene place of worship, it has been corrupted by demonic forces and turned into a blister of fel energy right on Astranaar's doorstep. Located southwest of Astranaar and west of the Ruins of Stardust, Fire Scar Shrine stands as a grim reminder of the Burning Legion's lingering poison in Ashenvale. The shrine has fallen under the sway of demonic corruption, nurtured by servants of the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council. Fel magic has twisted the surrounding earth into scorched rock, where roaming demons now gather in open defiance of the forest's defenders. The shrine's descent into darkness was spearheaded by agents like the orcish warlock Ilkrud Magthrull, operating under the orders of Athrikus Narassin. Though mortal sorcerers brought the corruption to bear, summoned fiends now patrol the altar stones unchecked. The localized tear in the veil occasionally draws greater horrors, including the towering doomguard Akkrilus.

subzone:forest-s-edge.text: Forest's Edge. Forest's Edge is a wooded wedge of land along the southwestern frontier of Elwynn Forest, flanked by rivers leading toward Westfall. Guarded to the north by Westbrook Garrison, this untamed area has become dangerously overrun by riverpaw gnolls under the command of the notorious Hogger. Tucked southwest of Stormwind City between Mirror Lake Orchard and the rivers bordering Westfall, Forest's Edge forms a natural peninsula of woodland. Despite its proximity to Westbrook Garrison, the Stormwind army's thin ranks have left the area vulnerable to wild beasts and raiding parties. Wandering boars roam among the trees and along the riverbanks, but the true menace is the concentration of Riverpaw gnolls who have made these woods their staging ground. The woods of Forest's Edge are the hunting grounds of Hogger, a massive and brutal gnoll chieftain. With a sizable bounty placed on his head by the Stormwind Army, Hogger directs his pack in harassing travelers and raiding nearby farms, turning what could be a peaceful timberland into a lethal proving ground for young Alliance adventurers.

subzone:forest-song.text: Forest Song. Forest Song is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in northeastern Ashenvale, near the tainted woods of Satyrnaar and the great portal at Bough Shadow. At present, it stands largely deserted save for the vigilant druid Kayneth Stillwind, who watches over the eastern border against emergent threats. Tucked away in the dense woodlands of northeastern Ashenvale, Forest Song was once an elegant settlement of the kaldorei. Today, white stone columns and crumbling archways are overgrown with ivy and wild ferns. Located northeast of Satyrnaar and just north of the encroaching Warsong Lumber Camp, the ruins hold a quiet, strategic overlook along the eastern trails toward Azshara and Bough Shadow. While the woods around it are plagued by demonic corruption and Horde incursions, the ruin itself maintains a haunting, tranquil stillness. Forest Song is currently manned solely by the druid Kayneth Stillwind. From this crumbling outpost, Stillwind keeps a watchful eye on the dark designs of enemies entering the wilderness, including the unsettling presence of the Forsaken in the eastern forests. Though isolated far from Astranaar and lacking garrison fortifications, the sanctuary serves as an important rallying point for Alliance travelers venturing toward the northern road into Felwood or investigating the corruptions seeping across the canopy.

subzone:forlorn-cavern.text: Forlorn Cavern. Tucked along the northern shores of Ironforge's subterranean lake, the Forlorn Cavern is a dimly lit, secluded district far removed from the city's bustling Great Forge. It serves as a shadowy refuge where thieves, cutpurses, and practitioners of the dark arts conduct their business away from prying dwarven guards. While the rest of Ironforge clangs with anvil strikes and radiates heat from the Great Forge, the Forlorn Cavern is cold, damp, and hushed. Wrapping along the northern edge of the mountain's underground lake, the winding pathways sit comfortably out of sight between the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Explorers. Its gloom makes it an ideal gathering place for those who prefer to keep their affairs discreet. Rogues and warlocks train here alongside vendors serving them, while weapon merchants and fishermen also work beside the lake.

subzone:frostmane-hold.text: Frostmane Hold. Frostmane Hold is a fortified encampment and cavern complex claimed by the Frostmane ice trolls in western Dun Morogh. Tucked into the crags south of Gnomeregan, it serves as a central staging ground for troll raiders encroaching on dwarven territory. The Ironforge Guard keeps a close watch on the hold to gauge the growing troll threat. Carved into the freezing cliffs of western Dun Morogh, Frostmane Hold consists of rough outdoor structures and a winding cave system. For the Frostmane tribe, it functions as a primary stronghold, densely guarded by hideskinners and headhunters. From here, the trolls launch raids into the surrounding valleys, testing the defenses of nearby settlements like Kharanos and menacing travelers along the mountain passes. As tensions in Dun Morogh mount, dwarven commanders in Kharanos have grown increasingly concerned about the scale of the Frostmane buildup. Young mountaineers and adventurers are routinely dispatched to scout the interior caverns, map out the defenses, and cull the warbands before the tribe can muster an organized assault against dwarven outposts.

subzone:furlbrow-s-pumpkin-farm.text: Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm. Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm is an overrun homestead in northern Westfall, just off the main road from Elwynn Forest. Once a prosperous plot tended by Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna, the fields and farmhouse have been seized by the Defias Brotherhood and prowling harvest golems. Situated near the northern border of Westfall, Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm was once known for producing robust crops to feed the kingdom. That ended when the Defias Brotherhood swept across the countryside. Outlaws drove Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna from their land, leaving their fields overrun with mechanical harvest golems programmed to attack anyone approaching. With the farm buildings occupied by bandits and the fields prowled by renegade machinery, the rightful owners have been forced to camp along the roadside near the Jansen Stead, mourning the loss of their home and livelihood. The farm's fall illustrates the broader collapse of law and order across Westfall. With Stormwind's military garrison spread thin and unable to safeguard rural freeholders, the Defias Brotherhood easily claimed homesteads like Furlbrow's. Bandits use the property as an staging ground and camp while letting lethal harvest watchers guard the perimeter, leaving travelers on the nearby highway vulnerable to ambush.

subzone:goblin-foundry.text: Goblin Foundry. The Goblin Foundry is an industrial workshop deep within the Deadmines where goblin tinkerers manufacture heavy metalwork for the Defias Brotherhood. A massive smelting cauldron dominates the chamber, which remains occupied by goblin craftsmen and engineers under Gilnid. Carved into the subterranean depths of Moonbrook, the Goblin Foundry provides the Defias Brotherhood with heavy manufacturing power. Goblin craftsmen and engineers work among the smelters and iron ramps, producing anchors and cannonballs. Gilnid presides over the foundry's goblin workforce. Craftsmen maintain production while engineers defend the workshop with remote-controlled golems, making its narrow ramps and molten metal dangerous for intruders.

subzone:gol-bolar-quarry-mine.text: Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine. Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine is an overrun excavation pit deep within the heart of Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. Originally worked by dwarven miners, the tunnels breached subterranean trogg caverns, unleashing a violent infestation that claimed the entire site. Today, the deepest shafts serve as the stronghold for the trogg warband led by the brute Hammerspine. The mine was established by Ironforge dwarves seeking stone and rich ore deposits beneath the craggy peaks of Dun Morogh. Work came to an abrupt, violent halt when pickaxes fractured a wall into an ancient subterranean cavern system inhabited by troggs. Swarming out from the dark, the subterranean beasts overwhelmed the work crews and forced a hasty retreat, ultimately spilling outward to overrun the surrounding quarry pit as well. While younger, weaker troggs roam the sunlit terraces of the quarry basin, the mine itself harbors the warband's fiercest fighters. Deep within these cramped, torchlit tunnels lurks their vicious chieftain, Hammerspine. Reclaiming the valuable quarry remains an urgent priority for the local mountaineers, but driving the infestation out requires venturing into the blackest depths of the mine to cut off the beasts at their source.

subzone:grand-vestibule.text: Grand Vestibule. The Grand Vestibule is the monumental entrance hall of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Lined with crimson pillars and stone effigies of fallen crusaders, it serves as the threshold where adventurers prepare to breach the monastery's inner halls. Past the heavy outer gates of the Monastery lies the Grand Vestibule, an expansive marble hall dedicated to the martial pride of the Scarlet Crusade. Statues of armored champions stand vigil beside vaulted stone pillars, and zealous sentries, disciples, and augurs patrol the flagstones to strike down anyone daring to enter without the order's crimson tabard. For trespassers, it is the first taste of the Crusade's unrelenting discipline and fanaticism. Because the vestibule sits directly outside the secured inner wings of the monastery, it functions as a perilous gathering point. Both Alliance strike teams sent north and Horde forces pushing out from the nearby Undercity converge under these high arches, turning the ornate entry into a chaotic and bloody battleground long before anyone breaches the inner cloisters.

subzone:great-forge.text: Great Forge. The Great Forge is the fiery heart and namesake of the dwarven capital of Ironforge. Situated at the very center of the city, its massive furnaces and famed Great Anvil never rest, producing legendary armaments and serving as the bustling center of civic life. The Great Forge was the very first structure built by the early dwarves beneath Ironforge Mountain, and the grand capital grew in concentric rings around it. Molten stone and slag pour constantly from giant foundries into glowing channels, illuminating the cavern with an amber haze. At its center stands the massive Great Anvil, overseen by Master of the Forge Myolor Sunderfury. Renowned masters of metalwork gather around its rim, hammering out armor, tools, and weapons day and night. Beyond its smithing operations, the Great Forge is the bustling crossroads of the entire mountain city. Ringed with guild offices, supply shops, and the city's primary gryphon roost maintained by Gryth Thurden, travelers from every corner of the Alliance mingle amid the clatter of hammers.

subzone:great-lift.text: Great Lift. The Great Lift is a massive, tauren-engineered elevator system perched on the southern edge of the Barrens. It serves as the primary route lowering travelers and supplies hundreds of feet into the sheer canyon basin of Thousand Needles. Despite its strategic value, aggressive quilboar encroaching through the southern wastes have made approaching the rim increasingly perilous. Spanning the sheer cliff edge between the southern Barrens and the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, the Great Lift stands as a marvel of practical tauren construction. Built using heavy timber, braided rope, and counterweighted pulleys, its paired platforms carry caravans, couriers, and warriors safely across a vertical precipice that would otherwise break any wagon. At the top and bottom platforms, tauren like Brave Moonhorn and Grish Longrunner maintain watch, keeping travelers informed of the road ahead and ensuring cargo passes smoothly. Operating the lift has become increasingly hazardous due to the hostile territory above it. Aggressive quilboar tribes in the southern Barrens have expanded aggressively southward, choking the road toward the lift and threatening to cut off Thousand Needles from the northern trails entirely. Those who make the long journey south must constantly fend off razorfen raiders before they can ever step foot onto the wooden platforms.

subzone:greatwood-vale.text: Greatwood Vale. Greatwood Vale is a forested valley nestled in the eastern foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via the perilous Webwinder Path. Recently, the hostile Grimtotem tribe seized the vale, using it as a staging ground for bloody assaults on neighboring settlements. Tucked away off the Webwinder Path, Greatwood Vale has become a violent frontier. The Grimtotem tribe, under the ruthless leadership of Grundig Darkcloud, has moved into the vale in force, cutting off safe passage and bringing terror to the surrounding foothills. The Grimtotem did not merely occupy Greatwood Vale; they used it to orchestrate the butchery of nearby Camp Aparaje. Sweeping out of the woods, Darkcloud's raiders slaughtered nearly every tauren inhabiting the encampment. Makaba Flathoof, one of the few survivors who managed to flee the carnage, now directs vengeful Horde warriors straight into the heart of Greatwood Vale to cut down the renegade Grimtotem and put an end to Grundig Darkcloud.

subzone:greenpaw-village.text: Greenpaw Village. Greenpaw Village is a furbolg settlement nestled in central Ashenvale, situated between Raynewood Retreat and Silverwind Refuge. It serves as the primary home of the Foulweald tribe, led by Chief Murgut and the shaman Oakpaw. Gripped by demonic corruption and embattled by outside forces, the village is an active conflict point for both Alliance and Horde travelers. Situated south of Raynewood Retreat and northeast of Silverwind Refuge, Greenpaw Village was once a quiet home for the forest's ursine denizens. In the wake of the Third War, its resident furbolgs—the Foulweald tribe—succumbed to the insidious corruption tainting Ashenvale's soil and spirits. Under the dominion of Chief Murgut and their corrupted spiritual guide, Shaman Oakpaw, the Foulweald have become hostile and unstable, attacking any travelers who stray into their forest territory. Because of their relentless aggression and proximity to major roadways, Greenpaw Village draws hostility from every side. Alliance sentinels and night elf druids seek to purge the mad furbolgs to protect their nearby outposts and sacred moonwells. Simultaneously, Horde forces advancing into Ashenvale have fought bloody skirmishes against the Foulweald as both factions push through the ancient woodland.

subzone:grim-batol.text: Grim Batol. Grim Batol is an ancient, ruined dwarven mountain fortress looming over the eastern edge of the Wetlands. Built by the Wildhammer clan, abandoned after a dark curse during the War of the Three Hammers, and later occupied by the Dragonmaw orcs as a dragon breeding lair, its sealed gates remain an ominous blight upon the highlands. Following the ancient civil war of the three clans, Thane Khardros Wildhammer carved Grim Batol out of the jagged mountains east of the marsh. During the subsequent War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud laid siege to the fortress. Although Khardros struck her down, Modgud cast a foul shadow across the stones before her death. The lingering taint rendered the halls uninhabitable, forcing the surviving Wildhammer dwarves to abandon their magnificent kingdom and migrate north into the Hinterlands. Centuries later during the Second War, the fortress found a darker purpose when Orgrim Doomhammer dispatched the Dragonmaw clan to claim it. Led by the warlock Nekros Skullcrusher, the orcs utilized the ancient artifact known as the Demon Soul to enslave the red Dragonqueen Alexstrasza deep within the mountain's roots. Forced to hatch broods for the Horde's war effort, Alexstrasza remained chained until a small band of heroes shattered the artifact. Once freed, the enraged Dragon Aspect incinerated the orcs within, leaving Grim Batol a smoldering, desolate ruin watched closely by surviving red dragons.

subzone:grizzled-den.text: Grizzled Den. The Grizzled Den is a cavern nestled in the snowy hills just southwest of Kharanos. It serves as a notorious lair for the ferocious, frost-breathing wendigos indigenous to Dun Morogh. Carved deep into the crags southwest of Kharanos, the Grizzled Den is notorious among local mountaineers as the nesting ground of Dun Morogh's wendigo packs. These aggressive, ape-like beasts wield frosty breath against intruders and band together to protect their hollows. Despite the peril, daring hunters regularly brave the cavern's depths to harvest thick wendigo manes, which fetch a respectable sum among craftsmen looking to line cold chairs and carriage seats with insulated fur. Beyond its fearsome inhabitants, the twisting tunnels of the Grizzled Den draw opportunists searching for natural wealth. Prospectors frequently venture past the outer entrance to hammer at copper veins jutting from the frozen stone walls, while adventurous scouts often scour the darker corners for discarded footlockers. However, delve too far into the inner reaches, and you are bound to face the dens' largest and most vicious predators lurking in the shadows.

subzone:grove-of-the-ancients.text: Grove of the Ancients. The Grove of the Ancients is a sacred night elven sanctuary set amidst old temple ruins in southeastern Darkshore. Nestled beside the Wildbend River, this serene haven serves as a gathering ground for nature spirits and is watched over by the venerable Ancient of Lore, Onu. Tucked away near the southeastern mountains of Darkshore, the Grove of the Ancients stands as a peaceful haven surrounded by aged temple stones. Through its heart flows the surging Wildbend River, providing a quiet refuge amidst a coastline increasingly plagued by corruption and restless wildlife. The grove serves as a meeting place for the Circle of Ancients, where nature spirits and kaldorei tend to the delicate balance of the forest. The focal presence within the grove is Onu, a towering Ancient of Lore who observes the land's shifting fortunes and offers ancient wisdom to passing travelers. Alongside Onu, wandering merchants and slumbering druids find rest beneath the boughs. Though quiet, the grove lies close to territorial furbolg camps to the southeast, making it an essential frontier outpost for Alliance sentinels and druids monitoring southern Darkshore.

subzone:gryphon-roost.text: Gryphon Roost. Perched along the ramparts just east of Stormwind's Trade District, the Gryphon Roost serves as the capital's primary transit hub for aerial travel. Managed by the human gryphon master Dungar Longdrink, it houses the majestic beasts that ferry couriers, soldiers, and adventurers across the Eastern Kingdoms.
